Separate aggregate from RegisteredUser (01) ON PURPOSE:
profile PII and password secrets live apart - a leak of one
table does not leak the other. Argon2id embeds the salt in
the hash string (no separate salt column). Never store or
access = JWT, 15 min, stateless, signed - the map API
refresh = 30 days, stored HASHED via RefreshTokenRepository
Reset flow (emailed 6-digit code - no URL link), three phases:
1. decide() - one consistent read+prune snapshot: unknown e-mail ->
SILENT no-op (still the same 200, anti-enumeration kept); the
provisioned admin (kind ADMIN) -> 403 NAMING the environment
provisioning (a code e-mailed to its address would let anyone who
finds the mailbox re-key the deployment); 60 s re-issue cooldown
(anchored at the latest row's createdAt - V8 rotation) + max 5 per
2. the send, OUTSIDE any transaction: a FRESH 6-digit code (shared
Codes.sixDigitCode(), same generator as contact-change); a REFUSED
send writes no token row and anchors no cooldown (the outage costs
the user nothing, the retry is not suppressed)
3. the write, one transaction (atomic one-active-code): delete the
user's prior active code, store {tokenHash = the KEYED,
domain-separated v2 hash (PiiCrypto.codeHash) of the code - a
6-digit space is brute-forceable from an unkeyed dump, the legacy
unkeyed SHA-256 form is still matched until its TTL, expiresAt =
4. the provisioned admin's e-mail is refused 403 first (no code can
be issued for it, and a direct call must not rewrite the env's
5. find the account's active code; verify attempts < 5 + hash match
(CodeHashes.matches - v2 or legacy, constant-time) + unused + not
expired; a wrong code PERSISTS its attempt increment (its failure
must not roll back the counter - reset() returns a boolean and the
controller answers the one generic 400 after the commit)
6. on success: hash the new password, update UserCredentials, mark
the code used (its hash is never re-usable, even before expiry),
revoke ALL refresh tokens for that user (stolen-session protection
Thin HTTP shell - zero logic, just wiring (Ch 1). permitAll = exactly
these 6 POST /auth/* endpoints (register, login, refresh, logout,
reads) + GET and HEAD /api/media/** (public media serving - the crisis
hero images; every other method stays authenticated) + actuator
health/info are the only other open routes; /swagger-ui + /v3/api-docs
are open in the dev/test profiles only (Profiles.isDevTestOnly - the
document is the full attack surface) - everything else is JWT (see
04-CONTEXT-AUTH wiring). Rate limiting (2026-09-08 hardened, SDI Ch 4
- /auth/register per client IP (account spam) PLUS a rolling
attempt counts, a 409 retry included; a hit
lands in the admin alert ring before the
- /auth/login per (IP, normalized contact) AND a per-IP
contact key = email lowercased or phone
- /auth/refresh + /auth/logout one SHARED session bucket per client IP
confirm code must not be brute-forceable
LocationController is defined in the shelter
context (05), listed here because it shares
compromise): changing the email requires an SMS code sent to the
CURRENT phone; changing the phone requires an email code sent to
the CURRENT email. Stealing only one channel is not enough.
One pending change per (user, type): resend cooldown (60 s),
code TTL (15 min), 5-attempt limit, duplicate target -> 409,
per-IP rate limit on the request endpoints.
profile = real profile + REAL verified claims + isAdmin (admin-moderation
D2): the frontend's single source of truth - the nav item and the /admin
route guard read isAdmin; it is the freshly loaded user's KIND (true only
for the ADMIN-kind row), never derived from any token claim.
ENV-PROVISIONED ADMIN (admin-moderation D1) - the admin comes from the
environment, never the registration flow (the mailbox does not exist and
1. Either ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD empty -> NO-OP. No admin exists,
/admin/* answers 403 for everyone (kind is the truth - a normal
account holding the email string stays a normal account), and the
app behaves exactly as without the capability (dev boxes without the
vars keep working; prod is opt-in).
2. A user with that email ALREADY exists (any kind; the lookup is
case-insensitive) -> NO-OP. The seeder NEVER re-hashes, flips kind or
touches claims - an in-app password change survives restarts and
kind ADMIN, name "Admin", NO phone (null - outside the partial unique
index, never a login route), no national ID code stored (M1 - the
pre-set SMART_ID claim carries the e-mail as its external ref),
true from the first request) + UserCredentials with the Argon2 hash
of ADMIN_PASSWORD (the same encoder registration uses).
Login is the NORMAL POST /auth/login (emailOrPhone + password) - no
dedicated endpoint, no backdoor, same JWT shape as every other user
(principal = userId, NO role claim - D2: /admin/* authorizes by a fresh
UserKind.ADMIN lookup per request, so a demotion takes effect on the very
OPS - de-provisioning: remove BOTH env vars AND delete the row (manual
SQL - no API deletes admin accounts). While both vars stay set, the
seeder RECREATES the admin on the next boot if the row was deleted
(create-if-absent sees no user with that email); with the vars removed it
is a no-op forever, but a still-existing row remains a working admin
(login with its own stored password) - row deletion is the real off switch.
Defined in 01 (app context). Shown here with the lookup
methods the auth context requires - contracts only.
6 buckets - register per IP; login per (IP, normalized contact) + per-IP aggregate; refresh + logout = session per IP; reset-request + reset-confirm per (IP, email)
per-e-mail rolling cap on registration ATTEMPTS ("register:" namespace; a hit lands in the alert ring, then 429 + Retry-After)
normalizes the login contact for the key (email lowercased; phone E.164 then lowercased)
